elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The chart shows total external debt from 2015 to 2025. Debt increased overall, from 2,103 to 5,621 US$ million, with the highest printed value in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.description: The stacked bars break down 2025 external debt by debt category and public and publicly guaranteed debt by creditor type. Private nonguaranteed debt is the largest main category at 2,449 US$ million, while multilateral creditors account for 1,143 of the 1,201 US$ million in public and publicly guaranteed debt. Other multilateral creditors are the largest multilateral component at 629, and other bilateral creditors are the smallest bilateral component at 1 US$ million.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show debt and debt-service ratios from 2015 to 2025 against shaded percentile ranges. In 2025, external debt to exports is the highest displayed ratio at 84%, while debt service to GNI is the lowest at 4%.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes show terms for official creditors and private creditors. Each box lists maturity, grace period and interest rate, with every value shown as '..' because there were no new commitments in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for official or private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
